answer_text: Under the Data Governance Act, the competent public sector body must decide within two months of receipt of the request; for exceptionally extensive and complex requests, that period may be extended by up to 30 days, with the applicant notified as soon as possible of the reasons for the delay.

Bribery Act 2010 (failure to prevent a bribe) - offence status and enforcement: NOT_FOUND

Modern Slavery Act 2015 (slavery and human trafficking statement) - enforcement: The duties imposed on commercial organisations by section 54 are enforceable by the Secretary of State bringing civil proceedings in the High Court for an injunction or, in Scotland, for specific performance of a statutory duty under section 45 of the Court of Session Act 1988 [14].

The Modern Slavery Act 2015 statement duty is not a criminal offence; it is enforced through civil proceedings brought by the Secretary of State (injunction in the High Court, or specific performance in Scotland). The evidence does not state whether the Bribery Act 2010 failure-to-prevent offence is criminal or how it is punished, so the two cannot be compared on that point.
